title: The Object With No Label
centralQuestion: What can we say about this object from the evidence — and what can't we say yet?

student.intro: This is a practice object. It is not from a real dig. Nobody knows what it is — there is no answer to find. Your job: say what you can SEE, say what you THINK, and say what is NOT proved. The Archive Apprentice will write your note.

terms.gloss: a line or cut on a surface
an opening that goes into or through something
what you can see or measure
to show something is definitely true

challenge: The ___ show(s) ___, but it does not prove ___.
Another idea is ___. To check, we would need ___.

evidence.label: Five small holes in a row
evidence.detail: Five round holes, about the same size, in a straight line along one edge.

evidence.label: One smooth side
evidence.detail: One side is smooth and shiny. The other side is rough.

evidence.label: It fits in one hand
evidence.detail: About 12 centimetres long. Light enough to hold in one hand.

evidence.label: Short marks near the holes
evidence.detail: Three short scratches next to the holes. They are not all the same length.

claims.text: The object was used as a tool
claims.doesNotProve: that the holes were made on purpose, or what the tool was for

claims.text: One side was rubbed smooth by use
claims.doesNotProve: that a person did the rubbing — water or sand can also make things smooth

claims.text: The marks were made to count something
claims.doesNotProve: that the marks were made on purpose, or what was counted

concepts.label: Describes the size or that it fits a hand
Suggests what the object was for
Links an idea to a piece of evidence with 'because'
Says what the evidence does NOT prove
Says what evidence would help next

prompts.firstTeach: Look at the object and the four pieces of evidence. Tell me what you can see, and what you think it was for.
prompts.reteach: Now explain the whole thing again in your own words: what you see, what you think, and what is not proved.
prompts.done: Your note is in the archive. Now teach a partner.

probes.text: What does this evidence not prove yet?
Why do you think that? Which piece of evidence?
Before we say what it was for — what exactly can you see?
What would we need to look at next to check your idea?

repairs.text: You said the evidence proves what it was. Can you make that more careful? Use 'but it does not prove'.
Good idea. Now add the evidence: 'I think ___ because ___'.

offLimits: what the object really is (there is no real answer)
dates, places, or a culture it came from
any evidence not in the four evidence cards
peerQuestion: Ask your partner: what is one thing the evidence does NOT prove?
